es: Leer un artículo de opinión y analizarlo: identificar la tesis, la postura y las concesiones, detectar suposiciones y apoyar cada inferencia en una pista del texto.

teaching.en: The thesis is the central claim a columnist wants you to accept, and it often returns, sharpened, in the last lines.
teaching.es: La tesis es la afirmación central que un columnista quiere que aceptes, y suele volver, más afilada, en las últimas líneas.
teaching.explanationEs: Thesis = tesis. Suele estar al principio o al final; busca verbos como argue, claim o maintain.
segments: The thesis is the central claim a columnist wants you to
accept, and it often returns, sharpened, in the last lines.
teaching.audioText: The thesis is the central claim a columnist wants you to accept, and it often returns, sharpened, in the last lines.

teaching.en: Admittedly, a good columnist will concede a point before replying, because a counterargument left unanswered can lend weight to the other side.
teaching.es: Es cierto que un buen columnista concede un punto antes de responder, porque un contraargumento sin respuesta puede dar peso al otro bando.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly anuncia una concesión; la postura del autor viene después de but o yet. Lend weight to = respaldar, dar peso.
segments: Admittedly, a good columnist will concede a point before replying, because
a counterargument left unanswered can lend weight to the other side.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, a good columnist will concede a point before replying, because a counterargument left unanswered can lend weight to the other side.

teaching.en: Writers who argue for a policy often rely on an underlying assumption, such as the belief that people always act rationally.
teaching.es: Quienes defienden una política suelen apoyarse en una suposición de fondo, como la creencia de que la gente siempre actúa racionalmente.
teaching.explanationEs: Underlying assumption = lo que se da por cierto sin decirlo. Palabras como always, obviously y everyone la delatan.
segments: Writers who argue for a policy often rely on an underlying
assumption, such as the belief that people always act rationally.
teaching.audioText: Writers who argue for a policy often rely on an underlying assumption, such as the belief that people always act rationally.

teaching.en: Readers infer a great deal from what a writer chooses to take for granted, because a sweeping generalisation hides beliefs nobody defends.
teaching.es: Los lectores infieren mucho de lo que el autor decide dar por sentado, porque una generalización excesiva esconde creencias que nadie defiende.
teaching.explanationEs: Infer = deducir algo que el texto no dice pero apoya. Sweeping generalisation: «todos», «nunca», «siempre» sin pruebas.
segments: Readers infer a great deal from what a writer chooses to
take for granted, because a sweeping generalisation hides beliefs nobody defends.
teaching.audioText: Readers infer a great deal from what a writer chooses to take for granted, because a sweeping generalisation hides beliefs nobody defends.

teaching.en: A one-sided article is easy to spot: it never mentions a counterargument, and its rhetorical questions leave no room for doubt.
teaching.es: Un artículo parcial es fácil de detectar: nunca menciona un contraargumento y sus preguntas retóricas no dejan margen a la duda.
teaching.explanationEs: One-sided = solo muestra un lado. Una pregunta retórica no espera respuesta: persuade, no demuestra.
segments: A one-sided article is easy to spot: it never mentions a
counterargument, and its rhetorical questions leave no room for doubt.
teaching.audioText: A one-sided article is easy to spot: it never mentions a counterargument, and its rhetorical questions leave no room for doubt.

teaching.en: If the evidence is weak, the thesis will not hold water, however confident the tone, and a careful reader says so.
teaching.es: Si las pruebas son débiles, la tesis no se sostendrá, por muy seguro que suene el tono, y un lector cuidadoso lo dice.
teaching.explanationEs: Hold water = resistir un examen (se usa sobre todo en negativa). El tono seguro no sustituye a las pruebas.
segments: If the evidence is weak, the thesis will not hold water,
however confident the tone, and a careful reader says so.
teaching.audioText: If the evidence is weak, the thesis will not hold water, however confident the tone, and a careful reader says so.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la tesis del autor en este fragmento?

choices.text: A daily tourist fee is a weaker idea than its supporters believe.
Tourists will pay any fee to visit a crowded old town.
Raising money from tourists is impossible in practice.

feedback.es: La tesis viene tras «But I would argue»: la tasa descansa en una suposición dudosa. «Visitors will pay anything» es la suposición que critica, y no afirma que recaudar sea imposible.

hint.es: La tesis es lo que defiende el autor, no lo que concede al principio.

origin.text: Charging tourists a daily fee is, admittedly, an easy way to raise money. But I would argue that it rests on a doubtful assumption: that visitors will pay anything to see the old town, however crowded it becomes.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por la palabra even, podemos inferir que antes rara vez lo hacía.»

feedback.es: Infer that… introduce una deducción apoyada en una pista; aquí even junto a now revela un cambio sorprendente.

hint.es: Es el verbo de deducir a partir de una pista.

origin.text: The columnist writes that even the mayor now cycles to work. From the word even, we can ___ that the mayor rarely did so before.

prompt.es: ¿Qué suposición da por cierta el autor sin demostrarla?

choices.text: That a ban on cars would be popular with most residents.
That cars are the main reason why customers reach the shops.
That shops could survive on online orders alone.

feedback.es: Decir que las tiendas siempre pierden clientes sin autos supone que los autos son el motivo principal de las visitas, y nadie lo demuestra. Las otras ideas no aparecen en la frase.

hint.es: Busca la idea que hace falta creer para que el «since» funcione.

origin.text: Since shops always lose customers when cars disappear, the ban is bound to go wrong.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué efecto busca la pregunta retórica de la autora.

choices.text: To show that the question has no clear answer.
To give the reader time to think before she offers evidence.
To make the reader share her answer before she argues it.

feedback.es: La autora contesta su propia pregunta: la retórica guía al lector hacia su tesis sin aportar datos. No deja la pregunta abierta ni da tiempo al lector: ella misma responde enseguida.

origin.audio: Who, exactly, benefits when a city turns its main square into a car park? Not the shopkeepers, who lose passing customers. Not the residents, who live with the noise. The writer does not wait for an answer. She supplies two, and moves on.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del artículo con la función que cumple.

pairs: Every driver wants a free road
Who would choose traffic over trees?

feedback.es: Cada frase tiene un papel distinto: concesión, generalización, persuasión y pista para deducir.

pairs: Every driver wants a free road
Who would choose traffic over trees?

prompt.es: Ordena: «La autora da por sentado lo que debería demostrar.»

answer.text: The writer takes for granted what she should prove

feedback.es: Takes for granted es el verbo habitual para lo que se supone sin demostrar; what she should prove introduce lo que falta por probar.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra la autora ante el proyecto del municipio?

choices.text: Openly angry: she accuses the council of wasting public money.
Neutral: she reports what the council says without comment.
Resigned: she accepts the lanes as the best the council can offer.
Mildly mocking: she doubts that the project is as bold as claimed.

feedback.es: «We are told», «Perhaps» y el detalle del alcalde llegando en auto revelan una burla suave: duda de que el plan sea tan audaz. No llega a la ira ni a la resignación, y tampoco es neutral.

origin.text: The council's new cycle lanes are, we are told, a bold step towards a greener future. Perhaps. They cost four million pounds, they end suddenly at the ring road, and on the day of the launch the mayor arrived by car, apparently because of the rain. One hopes the next step is better planned.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la columnista sobre los directivos.

choices.text: That they would change their minds if results were published.
That their opinion comes from habit rather than from evidence.
That they are inventing the anecdotes they keep repeating.

feedback.es: Denuncia una suposición (quien no se ve no trabaja), admite un abuso aislado y reprocha que todo se base en una anécdota: su opinión viene de la costumbre. No dice que mientan ni que cambiarían de opinión.

origin.audio: Much of the debate on working from home rests on a single assumption: that people who are not seen are not working. Admittedly, some employees do take advantage. But the evidence offered by managers is almost entirely anecdotal, and it is always the same anecdote, the colleague who was never online. A fair judgement would look at results, not at desks, and it would ask the employees themselves. Until then, the claim that remote work lowers performance will not hold water.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sin pruebas, su afirmación no se sostiene.»

feedback.es: Hold water es la colocación fija para un argumento que resiste el examen; en negativa indica que no se sostiene.

origin.text: The columnist says that cars cause most of the city's pollution. She offers no figures, only a picture of a traffic jam. Without evidence, her claim simply does not hold ___.

prompt.es: ¿Qué se puede inferir de «at present» y «only studying»?

choices.text: That the mayor has already decided against any ban.
That a ban may come later if the figures support it.
That the traffic figures are falling steadily, so the council needs no action.
That reporters have not been shown the figures.

feedback.es: «At present» y «only studying» dejan abierta la puerta a un cambio futuro; decir que las cifras son «very interesting» sugiere que podrían justificar una prohibición.

origin.text: We have no plans to ban cars from the old town, the mayor told reporters. At present, she added, the council is only studying the traffic figures, which, she said, are very interesting.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuál es la postura final de la autora.

choices.text: She understands the drivers' anger but keeps her position.
She accepts the drivers' complaints and concludes that the charge is wrong.
She dismisses the drivers' anger as exaggerated but defends the charge.

feedback.es: Concede la indignación («I do not dismiss their anger») y mantiene su tesis con «Even so». No cambia de opinión ni minimiza el enojo de los conductores.

origin.audio: I accept that many drivers feel punished by the new charge, and I do not dismiss their anger. Even so, I remain convinced that the charge is right, because the city centre has never been so crowded. The real question is not whether drivers are inconvenienced, but who should pay for the damage that traffic does.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe el lector esta carta?

choices.text: To support the columnist's view that libraries are too expensive.
To accuse the columnist of being dishonest with her readers and the council.
To propose a detailed plan for funding small libraries.
To reframe the question in order to persuade the council.

feedback.es: Cambia la pregunta de la columnista por otra («whether we can afford to close them») y termina pidiendo al municipio que reconsidere: su propósito es persuadir. No respalda a la columnista, no la acusa ni detalla un plan.

origin.text: Letters page: Sir, your columnist asks whether we can afford to keep our small libraries open. The better question is whether we can afford to close them. Every library that shuts is a door that a child will never open. I urge the council to think again.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es una pregunta retórica destinada a ganarse al lector.»

feedback.es: Una pregunta retórica no busca información: persuade al lector para que llegue a la respuesta del autor.

origin.text: Who could possibly object to cleaner air? The writer does not expect an answer; it is a ___ question meant to win the reader over.

es: Revisar un borrador y corregir seis problemas de registro, cohesión y matiz, cambiando lo vago por datos exactos y las afirmaciones exageradas por otras ajustadas.

teaching.en: In an email to the director, a formal register opens with Dear Ms Lopez, not Hi all, and avoids slang.
teaching.es: En un correo a la directora, un registro formal empieza con Dear Ms Lopez, no con Hi all, y evita la jerga.
teaching.explanationEs: Register: el saludo y las palabras deben encajar con quien lee.
segments: In an email to the director, a formal register opens
with Dear Ms Lopez, not Hi all, and avoids slang.
teaching.audioText: In an email to the director, a formal register opens with Dear Ms Lopez, not Hi all, and avoids slang.

teaching.en: To hedge a claim, write 'many students seem to dislike it', because 'everyone hates it' would overstate the evidence.
teaching.es: Para matizar una afirmación, escribe «a muchos estudiantes parece no gustarles», porque «todos lo odian» exageraría la evidencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Overstate = exagerar. Sustituye todos/nadie por many/some y añade seem to o appear to.
segments: To hedge a claim, write 'many students seem to dislike
it', because 'everyone hates it' would overstate the evidence.
teaching.audioText: To hedge a claim, write 'many students seem to dislike it', because 'everyone hates it' would overstate the evidence.

teaching.en: A linker such as however or so gives a text cohesion, whereas a run-on sentence joins ideas with nothing but commas.
teaching.es: Un conector como however o so da cohesión a un texto, mientras que una oración encadenada une ideas solo con comas.
teaching.explanationEs: Cohesion: los conectores (so, however, although) enlazan ideas. Run-on sentence: «The price rose, students complained» necesita linker o punto.
segments: A linker such as however or so gives a text cohesion,
whereas a run-on sentence joins ideas with nothing but commas.
teaching.audioText: A linker such as however or so gives a text cohesion, whereas a run-on sentence joins ideas with nothing but commas.

teaching.en: Vague words like soon or several should become precise details, such as by Friday or three complaints.
teaching.es: Las palabras vagas como soon o several deben convertirse en datos precisos, como by Friday o three complaints.
teaching.explanationEs: Vague = impreciso. Un plazo con fecha y una cifra son más útiles que un adverbio.
segments: Vague words like soon or several should become precise
details, such as by Friday or three complaints.
teaching.audioText: Vague words like soon or several should become precise details, such as by Friday or three complaints.

teaching.en: When you revise a draft, tighten up the wording by cutting filler, but do not water down the point you are making.
teaching.es: Al revisar un borrador, ajusta la redacción eliminando el relleno, pero no diluyas la idea que defiendes.
teaching.explanationEs: Tighten up = hacer más conciso. Water down = rebajar la fuerza de una idea; matizar no es diluir.
segments: When you revise a draft, tighten up the wording by cutting
filler, but do not water down the point you are making.
teaching.audioText: When you revise a draft, tighten up the wording by cutting filler, but do not water down the point you are making.

teaching.en: Every change must earn its place: if a new word is merely a synonym and adds nothing, leave the draft as it was.
teaching.es: Cada cambio debe justificarse: si una palabra nueva es solo un sinónimo y no aporta nada, deja el borrador como estaba.
teaching.explanationEs: Un cambio vale solo si mejora el registro, la cohesión o el matiz.
segments: Every change must earn its place: if a new word is merely
a synonym and adds nothing, leave the draft as it was.
teaching.audioText: Every change must earn its place: if a new word is merely a synonym and adds nothing, leave the draft as it was.

prompt.es: ¿Qué corrección mejora el registro del saludo a la directora?

choices.text: Hello everybody, I am writing about the school canteen.
Dear Ms Lopez, I am writing about the school canteen.
Dear Ms Lopez, hiya, I am writing about the school canteen.

feedback.es: El saludo debe dirigirse a la persona que lee y mantenerse formal de principio a fin. Hello everybody sigue siendo informal, y la tercera mezcla registros.

hint.es: Piensa a quién va dirigido el mensaje: la directora.

origin.text: Draft: Hi all! I am writing about the school canteen, because the food is a problem and the director must read this today.

prompt.es: Completa: «A muchos estudiantes parece no gustarles el nuevo menú.»

feedback.es: Seem to + verbo matiza la afirmación: no dice que todos lo odian, sino que parece que a muchos no les gusta.

hint.es: Es el verbo que atenúa: «parece que», no «es seguro que».

origin.text: The survey covered only thirty students from one class, so the writer should not overstate the result. A more careful version is: Many students ___ to dislike the new menu.

prompt.es: ¿Qué reescritura sustituye lo vago por datos precisos?

choices.text: We will ask the director very soon, and many students have already complained.
We will ask the director in due course, and some students have already complained.
We will ask the director by Friday, and three students have already complained.

feedback.es: Un día y una cifra son datos precisos. «Very soon», «many», «in due course» y «some» suenan distinto, pero siguen sin decir cuándo ni cuántos.

hint.es: Un dato preciso es un día y una cifra, no un adverbio más formal.

origin.text: Draft: We will ask the director soon, and several students have already complained.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aunque el precio ha subido, muchos estudiantes parecen satisfechos.»

answer.text: Although the price has risen many students seem satisfied
accepted: Although the price has risen many students seem satisfied
Many students seem satisfied although the price has risen

feedback.es: Although une las dos ideas en una sola frase y seem matiza la segunda; el orden inverso con la subordinada al final también es correcto.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué consigue la editora con el cambio.

choices.text: She makes the claim easier to support without changing its direction.
She removes the writer's criticism of the rule completely.
She adds survey evidence that supports the original claim.

feedback.es: Cambia «disaster» y «nobody» por «some families» y «few parents»: la dirección es la misma, pero ahora se puede probar. No elimina la crítica ni añade datos de una encuesta: ajusta las palabras.

origin.audio: The first draft said that the new rule was a disaster and that nobody supported it. The editor replaced both phrases: the rule has caused problems for some families, and few parents have spoken in its favour. The meaning is similar, but the claim is now one that the writer can back up with evidence.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada edición con el problema que corrige.

pairs: The price rose. Students complained. → The price rose, so students complained.

pairs.es: Mejora la cohesión con un conector

pairs: Everyone hates it → Many seem to dislike it
We will ask soon → We will ask by Friday

pairs.es: Sustituye lo vago por un dato preciso

feedback.es: Cada edición corrige un problema distinto: registro, cohesión, exageración y vaguedad.

pairs: The price rose. Students complained. → The price rose, so students complained.

pairs.es: Mejora la cohesión con un conector

pairs: Everyone hates it → Many seem to dislike it
We will ask soon → We will ask by Friday

pairs.es: Sustituye lo vago por un dato preciso

prompt.es: ¿Qué lista resume los problemas principales del borrador?

choices.text: A casual greeting, overstated claims, a vague deadline and several factual errors.
A casual greeting, overstated claims, a vague deadline and very short sentences.
A casual greeting, cautious claims, a vague deadline and repeated ideas.

feedback.es: Abre con «Hi all», exagera («everyone hates it», «obviously»), deja un plazo vago («soon») y encadena frases cortas sin conectores. No hay errores de hechos señalables ni afirmaciones cautas.

origin.text: Hi all. The school food is terrible and everyone hates it. The new menu is obviously better. Students like it. The price went up. The cooks say they are sorry. We must change the menu now. The director must read this today. We will ask her soon. Last week, two students were ill after lunch. The parents are angry. Nobody wants to wait in a long line. The teachers say that the new menu has fewer vegetables, and some parents say that it costs too much. Thank you.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la editora suaviza la segunda frase.

choices.text: Because the director dislikes strong opinions.
Because the claim was not formal enough.
Because the survey only supports a weaker claim.

feedback.es: Suaviza porque la encuesta solo respalda «many students seem to dislike»: el matiz ajusta la frase a la evidencia, no al gusto de la directora ni al registro.

origin.audio: I changed the greeting from Hi all to Dear Ms Lopez, because the reader is the director. Then I softened the second sentence. Everyone hates the food became many students seem to dislike the food, which the survey actually supports. Finally, I joined the two short sentences with so, and I replaced soon with by Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para dejar el texto más conciso, hay que recortar dos frases.»

feedback.es: Tighten up es la colocación natural para hacer un texto más conciso eliminando lo que sobra.

origin.text: The second paragraph repeats the same point three times. To ___ up the text, the writer should cut two of the sentences and keep the clearest one.

prompt.es: Reescribe el borrador como un solo mensaje formal a la directora.

answer.text: Dear Ms Lopez, many students seem to dislike the canteen food, and the price has risen, so we would be grateful if you could review the menu by Friday.
accepted: Dear Ms Lopez, many students seem to dislike the canteen food, and the price has risen, so we would be grateful if you could review the menu by Friday.
Dear Ms Lopez, it appears that many students dislike the canteen food, and the price has gone up; therefore, we would ask you to change the menu by Friday.
Dear Ms Lopez, some students seem unhappy with the food in the canteen, and the price has risen, so please review the menu before Friday.

feedback.es: Un mensaje editado abre con saludo formal, matiza «everyone hates» con seem to o many, une las ideas con un conector y fija un plazo exacto.

origin.text: Hi all. The canteen food is terrible and everyone hates it. The price went up. We will ask the director soon. Nobody listens to us.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión aporta cohesión y deja claro el contraste?

choices.text: The price rose; however, students still seem to like the menu, and the cooks say they are sorry.
The price rose, students still like the menu, the cooks say they are sorry.
The price rose, so students still seem to like the menu, and the cooks say they are sorry.

feedback.es: However marca el contraste y and suma la última idea. La versión con solo comas es una oración encadenada, y la que usa so establece una causa ilógica.

origin.text: Draft: The price rose. Students still like the menu. The cooks say they are sorry.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué principio aplica la editora.

choices.text: That negative results should never appear in formal writing.
That a precise figure is stronger than an exaggerated judgement.
That a complaint only counts if a majority makes it.

feedback.es: Las preguntas de la editora sustituyen un juicio exagerado por un dato (doce de doscientos). No se prohíbe lo negativo ni se exige una mayoría.

origin.audio: An editor reads a line in a draft: the results were obviously terrible. She asks the writer what exactly was terrible, how many people said so, and compared with what. The writer replies that only twelve parents complained out of two hundred. Together they change the sentence to: a small number of parents complained, and the school plans to reply by Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «No quisimos diluir el punto principal.»

feedback.es: Water down significa rebajar la fuerza de una idea; tone down y play down son alternativas naturales.

origin.text: The director asked us to change the wording of our request, but we refused to ___ down the main point: the menu must change.

es: Sintetizar la información de un audio y de un texto: comparar lo que coincide, señalar las discrepancias y cerrar con una conclusión.

teaching.en: According to the radio report, the library closes in June, whereas the newspaper claims that it closes in July.
teaching.es: Según el informe de la radio, la biblioteca cierra en junio, mientras que el periódico afirma que cierra en julio.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas contrasta dos fuentes: cada una con su dato, en una sola frase.
segments: According to the radio report, the library closes in June,
whereas the newspaper claims that it closes in July.
teaching.audioText: According to the radio report, the library closes in June, whereas the newspaper claims that it closes in July.

teaching.en: Both sources report a fall in visits, and likewise both attribute it to the new opening hours.
teaching.es: Las dos fuentes informan de una caída de visitas y, del mismo modo, ambas la atribuyen al nuevo horario.
teaching.explanationEs: Both + fuentes en plural + verbo sin -s. Likewise añade otra coincidencia.
segments: Both sources report a fall in visits, and likewise
both attribute it to the new opening hours.
teaching.audioText: Both sources report a fall in visits, and likewise both attribute it to the new opening hours.

teaching.en: The radio figure does not tally with the newspaper's, so a careful listener will cross-check both against the official record.
teaching.es: La cifra de la radio no coincide con la del periódico, así que un oyente cuidadoso contrastará las dos con el registro oficial.
teaching.explanationEs: Tally with = coincidir. Cross-check = contrastar con una segunda fuente. Figure = cifra.
segments: The radio figure does not tally with the newspaper's, so
a careful listener will cross-check both against the official record.
teaching.audioText: The radio figure does not tally with the newspaper's, so a careful listener will cross-check both against the official record.

teaching.en: When two conflicting accounts give different dates, name the discrepancy first and only then try to reconcile it.
teaching.es: Cuando dos versiones contradictorias dan fechas distintas, nombra la discrepancia primero y solo entonces intenta conciliarlas.
teaching.explanationEs: Discrepancy = diferencia entre datos. Reconcile = mostrar que dos datos pueden ser compatibles.
segments: When two conflicting accounts give different dates, name the
discrepancy first and only then try to reconcile it.
teaching.audioText: When two conflicting accounts give different dates, name the discrepancy first and only then try to reconcile it.

teaching.en: Judge each source by asking who is speaking, what they know and whether they gain from your believing them.
teaching.es: Juzga cada fuente preguntándote quién habla, qué sabe y si gana algo con que tú le creas.
teaching.explanationEs: Evaluar la fuente: quién habla, qué sabe y qué interés tiene. Es parte de una buena síntesis.
segments: Judge each source by asking who is speaking, what they
know and whether they gain from your believing them.
teaching.audioText: Judge each source by asking who is speaking, what they know and whether they gain from your believing them.

teaching.en: Taken together, the two sources agree on the problem, and overall the discrepancy concerns only the date.
teaching.es: En conjunto, las dos fuentes coinciden en el problema y, globalmente, la discrepancia afecta solo a la fecha.
teaching.explanationEs: Taken together y overall abren la conclusión: resumen coincidencias y diferencias en una frase.
segments: Taken together, the two sources agree on the problem,
and overall the discrepancy concerns only the date.
teaching.audioText: Taken together, the two sources agree on the problem, and overall the discrepancy concerns only the date.

prompt.es: Escucha la radio, lee el aviso y elige en qué discrepan las dos fuentes.

choices.text: The cost of the playground.
Whether the playground will be built at all.
The month in which the playground will open.

feedback.es: La radio dice mayo y el aviso del municipio dice junio: esa es la discrepancia. El aviso no da cifra, así que no contradice el coste, y las dos fuentes suponen que el parque se construirá.

hint.es: Compara el mes que da cada fuente.

origin.audio: The mayor says the new playground will open in May, and that it will cost two hundred thousand pounds.
origin.text: Council notice: The new playground will open in June. The final cost will be confirmed when the building work is complete.

prompt.es: Completa: «La radio dice cuatrocientos, mientras que el periódico da trescientos.»

feedback.es: Whereas une en una sola frase dos datos que se contrastan; while también es posible con este sentido.

hint.es: Es el conector que contrasta dos fuentes en una frase.

origin.text: The radio report says that four hundred people attended the march, ___ the newspaper gives three hundred. Nobody explains the difference.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En conjunto, ambas fuentes coinciden en el problema.»

answer.text: Overall both sources agree on the problem

feedback.es: Overall abre la conclusión; both sources lleva verbo en plural sin -s (agree).

hint.es: La conclusión empieza con el conector que resume.

prompt.es: ¿Qué valoración de las dos fuentes es la más acertada?

choices.text: B is better supported, but its figure is still an estimate.
A is more reliable because the owner was present.
Neither can be used because the two sources disagree.

feedback.es: La estimación apoyada en fotos es más sólida que un recuerdo impreciso, pero sigue siendo una estimación. Estar presente no garantiza exactitud, y una discrepancia no anula todas las fuentes.

origin.text: Source A: a shop owner says that hundreds of people joined the march. Source B: the police estimate, based on photographs taken from above, is three thousand.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con la función que cumple en una síntesis.

pairs.es: Contrasta dos datos en una sola frase
Añade otra coincidencia entre las fuentes
Coincidir con el dato de otra fuente
Resume lo que aportan las dos fuentes

feedback.es: Cada expresión cumple una función distinta: contrastar, sumar coincidencias, comprobar y resumir.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo se relacionan las dos fuentes.

choices.text: They disagree about the size of the fall, and only one gives a cause.
They agree more or less on the size of the fall, but neither gives a cause.
They agree on the cause of the fall, although the figures are quite different from each other.

feedback.es: Un quinto y el dieciocho por ciento son cifras parecidas, y ninguna fuente explica el motivo. Las otras opciones inventan un desacuerdo o una causa.

origin.audio: The report on the radio says that visits to the library fell last year by about a fifth. The figure in the newspaper article is similar: it speaks of a drop of eighteen per cent. Neither source explains why the fall happened.

prompt.es: Escucha la radio, lee la noticia y elige qué se puede concluir de las dos versiones.

choices.text: They agree on the numbers of users, but differ on the dates of the closure.
They agree on everything except who will be responsible for the repairs.
They agree that the pool will close, but differ on dates and numbers.

feedback.es: Ambas hablan del cierre por reparaciones; la radio da junio-septiembre y unos cuatrocientos socios, y el periódico julio-octubre y unos trescientos: difieren en fechas y en cifras. No se habla de quién paga.

origin.audio: A local radio station reported this morning that the swimming pool will close for repairs in June and reopen in September. The manager told the station that about four hundred members use the pool every week, and that most of them are older people who have no other place to exercise.
origin.text: Town Gazette: The swimming pool will close from July for essential repairs, the council has confirmed. Around three hundred people use it each week, according to council records, and the work is expected to last until October.

prompt.es: ¿Qué podría explicar que la cifra de la radio sea mayor?

choices.text: The radio figure includes visitors who do not pay.
The manager has overstated the number of users to help his case.
The newspaper has mixed up its records of members and visitors.

feedback.es: El gerente cuenta a todos los que entran y el registro solo las entradas de pago: esa diferencia de método explica la discrepancia sin acusar a nadie. No hay pruebas de mala fe ni de que el periódico confundiera sus registros.

origin.text: The radio figure comes from the pool manager, who counts every member at the door. The newspaper figure comes from council records, which count only paid entries.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las dos estimaciones no coinciden entre sí.»

feedback.es: Tally with es la colocación habitual para cifras que cuadran; agree with o match with también son naturales.

origin.text: One report says four hundred people use the pool each week, and another says three hundred. The two estimates simply do not ___ with each other.

prompt.es: Escucha, lee y escribe una síntesis que compare la fecha y el número de pasajeros.

answer.text: According to the radio, the night bus will stop in March, whereas the newspaper says that it will be cut from April. Both sources agree that the company is ending the service, but they differ on the number of passengers: about thirty, according to the company, against nearly eighty, according to the campaign group. Overall, the discrepancy over the date and the figures suggests that the two sides are using different data.
accepted: According to the radio, the night bus will stop in March, whereas the newspaper says that it will be cut from April. Both sources agree that the company is ending the service, but they differ on the number of passengers: about thirty, according to the company, against nearly eighty, according to the campaign group. Overall, the discrepancy over the date and the figures suggests that the two sides are using different data.

The radio says the night bus will stop running in March, but the article gives April. The two sources agree that the service is ending, while they disagree about how many people use it: thirty, according to the company, and eighty, according to the campaign group. Taken together, the sources show a real discrepancy, and the figures may come from different counts.

feedback.es: Una buena síntesis compara en un párrafo: fecha de cada fuente, lo que coincide, cifras en contraste y una conclusión con overall o taken together.

origin.text: Article. Evening Post: The night bus on route twelve will be cut from April, the company has confirmed. A campaign group says that nearly eighty people use it every night, mostly hospital staff, and they have collected two thousand signatures.
origin.audio: The transport company announced today that the night bus on route twelve will stop running from March, because only about thirty passengers use it each night. A spokesperson added that a taxi service may replace it.

prompt.es: Escucha la radio, lee el texto y elige cómo se relacionan las dos fuentes.

choices.text: The text confirms the radio figure and shows that it applies to all workers.
The text supports the radio figure but limits how far it applies.
The text adds a cause that the radio did not mention.

feedback.es: El 21 por ciento coincide con «uno de cada cinco», y la advertencia sobre la muestra limita su alcance. El texto no generaliza a todos los trabajadores ni menciona una causa.

origin.audio: Researchers told a radio show that about one in five commuters now works from home at least three days a week.
origin.text: Transport Weekly: A new survey of two thousand commuters finds that twenty-one per cent work from home at least three days a week, although the authors warn that the sample came mainly from city offices.

prompt.es: ¿Qué concluye la autora sobre las dos noticias?

choices.text: That the sources do not really conflict, because they refer to different events.
That one source is clearly more reliable than the other, and should be trusted.
That the date is unknown, so the reports cannot be compared.
That both sources made a mistake in reporting the date.

feedback.es: «Smaller than it looks» significa que la discrepancia es solo aparente: hablan de hechos distintos. No declara una fuente más fiable ni imposible la comparación.

origin.text: The two reports differ on the date, but a closer look shows that the radio gave the start of the works, whereas the newspaper gave the date of the official opening. The discrepancy is therefore smaller than it looks.

prompt.es: Completa: «Del mismo modo, el periódico lo describió como una clara mejora.»

feedback.es: Likewise añade una coincidencia entre las fuentes; Similarly tiene el mismo sentido en este contexto.

origin.text: The radio report praised the new timetable for its reliability. ___, the newspaper described it as a clear improvement on the old one.

es: Responder a un dilema con una estructura clara (postura, razón, ejemplo y matiz) y manejar una pregunta inesperada ganando tiempo con naturalidad.

teaching.en: An ethical dilemma has no perfect answer, so strike a balance: give your position first and say what it comes down to.
teaching.es: Un dilema ético no tiene respuesta perfecta, así que busca un equilibrio: da primero tu postura y di a qué se reduce todo.
teaching.explanationEs: Balance = equilibrio. It comes down to + lo esencial de la decisión.
segments: An ethical dilemma has no perfect answer, so strike a balance:
give your position first and say what it comes down to.
teaching.audioText: An ethical dilemma has no perfect answer, so strike a balance: give your position first and say what it comes down to.

teaching.en: The money from a sponsor can help a small club, but it can cut both ways if the donor expects something in return.
teaching.es: El dinero de un patrocinador puede ayudar a un club pequeño, pero puede tener su doble filo si el donante espera algo a cambio.
teaching.explanationEs: Cut both ways = tener ventajas e inconvenientes. Sponsor = patrocinador.
segments: The money from a sponsor can help a small club, but it
can cut both ways if the donor expects something in return.
teaching.audioText: The money from a sponsor can help a small club, but it can cut both ways if the donor expects something in return.

teaching.en: For instance, a sweet-drink company sponsoring a health club creates a conflict of interest that the club must acknowledge.
teaching.es: Por ejemplo, una empresa de bebidas dulces que patrocina un club de salud crea un conflicto de intereses que el club debe reconocer.
teaching.explanationEs: For instance introduce un caso concreto que sostiene la razón. Conflict of interest = conflicto de intereses.
segments: For instance, a sweet-drink company sponsoring a health club creates
a conflict of interest that the club must acknowledge.
teaching.audioText: For instance, a sweet-drink company sponsoring a health club creates a conflict of interest that the club must acknowledge.

teaching.en: Make your answer fair by granting the other side its best point, and only then say where you would draw the line.
teaching.es: Haz tu respuesta justa reconociendo el mejor punto del otro lado, y solo entonces di dónde pondrías el límite.
teaching.explanationEs: Fair = justo. Draw the line = fijar el límite que no se cruza.
segments: Make your answer fair by granting the other side its best
point, and only then say where you would draw the line.
teaching.audioText: Make your answer fair by granting the other side its best point, and only then say where you would draw the line.

teaching.en: That said, you may accept a proposal and still set one condition, because a condition refines a position without reversing it.
teaching.es: Dicho esto, puedes aceptar una propuesta y aun así poner una condición, porque una condición afina la postura sin invertirla.
teaching.explanationEs: That said abre el matiz. Una condición (provided that…) no cambia tu postura: la precisa.
segments: That said, you may accept a proposal and still set one
condition, because a condition refines a position without reversing it.
teaching.audioText: That said, you may accept a proposal and still set one condition, because a condition refines a position without reversing it.

teaching.en: If a question is unexpected, gain a moment with That is a fair point, then answer in the same four steps.
teaching.es: Si una pregunta es inesperada, gana un momento con «Es un punto acertado» y responde en los mismos cuatro pasos.
teaching.explanationEs: Frases para ganar tiempo: That is a fair point / Let me think for a moment. Después, postura, razón, ejemplo y matiz.
segments: If a question is unexpected, gain a moment with That is
a fair point, then answer in the same four steps.
teaching.audioText: If a question is unexpected, gain a moment with That is a fair point, then answer in the same four steps.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta sigue la estructura postura + razón + ejemplo?

choices.text: That is a difficult question, and there are many things to consider before any decision is made.
I would accept, but then again I would refuse, because both choices have clear advantages and some real disadvantages.
Banks usually sponsor events because they want attention and new customers for their services.
I would accept, because the fair needs funding; for instance, last year we had no budget for materials.

feedback.es: Es la única respuesta que toma postura, la justifica con because y aporta un ejemplo concreto con for instance. Las demás no toman postura o se contradicen.

hint.es: Busca una postura clara, una razón y un caso concreto.

origin.text: Dilemma: a bank offers to sponsor the school science fair, but it wants its name on every poster.

prompt.es: Completa: «Dicho esto, aun así aceptaría al patrocinador.»

feedback.es: That said abre el matiz: concede el punto de los padres sin cambiar la postura, que sigue siendo aceptar.

hint.es: Son dos palabras que abren un matiz; falta la primera.

origin.text: I understand why some parents oppose the plan, and I share part of their concern. ___ said, I would still accept the sponsor, provided that the club keeps control of the team.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En conjunto, yo aceptaría la oferta con dos condiciones.»

answer.text: On balance I would accept the offer with two conditions

feedback.es: On balance abre la postura sopesada y with two conditions añade el matiz sin invertirla.

hint.es: Empieza con la expresión que resume el balance de ventajas y riesgos.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo maneja Sara la pregunta inesperada.

choices.text: She pauses to think but then avoids taking a clear position.
She buys a moment and then answers in her usual structure.
She answers firmly and never acknowledges the objection.

feedback.es: Sara usa «a fair point» para ganar tiempo y responde con postura (rechazar), razón (adolescentes) y matiz (algo neutral). No esquiva la pregunta ni ignora la objeción.

origin.audio: Asked whether her club should accept money from an oil company, Sara paused and said that this was a fair point. She explained that she would refuse, because the club works with teenagers, and that she would draw the line at any advertising near the pitch. Only then did she add that the company might give money to something neutral, such as repairing the roof.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada parte de la respuesta con su función.

pairs: For instance, the nets are broken
That said, I would set one condition

feedback.es: Cada parte cumple una función distinta: postura, razón, ejemplo y matiz.

pairs: For instance, the nets are broken

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta gana tiempo de forma natural ante la pregunta del entrevistador?

choices.text: That would never happen, so I do not really need to answer that kind of question.
Well, it depends on the amount of money, and I would decide later when we know more.
That is a fair point; let me think for a moment.

feedback.es: Reconocer el punto y pedir un momento es una forma natural de ganar tiempo antes de responder. Las otras dos esquivan la pregunta o evitan tomar postura.

origin.text: Interviewer: Would you still accept the money if the sponsor asked you to drop one player from the team?

prompt.es: Responde al dilema como si hablaras dos minutos y contesta a la pregunta inesperada.

answer.text: To begin with, I would accept the sponsor, because our club needs new equipment and the school cannot pay for it. For instance, the nets are broken, and half of the balls are old. On balance, I think the benefits outweigh the risks, although I see the dilemma: the café sells sweet drinks, and our club is about health. It comes down to whether we can accept the money without losing our values. That said, I would set two conditions. First, the café must also sell water and fruit at our events. Second, the sponsor cannot decide anything about the team. As for your question about the logo, that is a fair point. Let me think for a moment. I would accept a small logo on the shirts, provided that the players agree and the logo stays small. That is where I would draw the line: no advertising during matches. In short, I would say yes, but only with clear limits, and I would review the agreement at the end of the season.
accepted: To begin with, I would accept the sponsor, because our club needs new equipment and the school cannot pay for it. For instance, the nets are broken, and half of the balls are old. On balance, I think the benefits outweigh the risks, although I see the dilemma: the café sells sweet drinks, and our club is about health. It comes down to whether we can accept the money without losing our values. That said, I would set two conditions. First, the café must also sell water and fruit at our events. Second, the sponsor cannot decide anything about the team. As for your question about the logo, that is a fair point. Let me think for a moment. I would accept a small logo on the shirts, provided that the players agree and the logo stays small. That is where I would draw the line: no advertising during matches. In short, I would say yes, but only with clear limits, and I would review the agreement at the end of the season.

My position is that we should accept the money. The club is small, and it needs new equipment. For example, we have only one good ball, and the shirts are very old. The school cannot pay for new things, so the help of a sponsor is important to us. Although the café sells sweet drinks, we can ask it to offer water as well. It comes down to trust: if the sponsor respects our conditions, the agreement can work. That said, I would want a written agreement, because the sponsor should not choose our team. About the logo, good question. Let me think. I would accept it on the shirts, as long as the players agree, but I would draw the line at advertising during matches. I would also ask the players and the families for their opinion before we sign anything. Overall, I would say yes, with clear limits.

feedback.es: Una respuesta completa da la postura, la razón con un ejemplo, un matiz con condiciones y contesta la pregunta inesperada con calma y en la misma estructura.

origin.text: Dilema: un café local ofrece patrocinar el club deportivo de tu escuela, pero vende bebidas dulces. Responde como si hablaras durante dos minutos: postura, razón con ejemplo y matiz. Después contesta a la pregunta inesperada: «¿Y si el café quisiera poner su logotipo en las camisetas?»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué muestra la última frase de la hablante.

choices.text: That her acceptance comes with a limit she will not cross.
That she has changed her mind about accepting the money.
That she believes the company's name is not a problem for young people.

feedback.es: «That said, I would insist…» añade una condición sin cambiar la postura: acepta, pero con un límite. No rectifica ni cree inocua la marca.

origin.audio: Some people say that a sports club should never accept money from a company that sells fast food, and I see the risk. But I would argue that refusing would hurt the children more than the company's name would, because the club is small and its members are young. For instance, last year our club cancelled two tournaments for lack of funds. That said, I would insist that the company does not appear on the children's shirts.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta mantiene la estructura ante la pregunta inesperada?

choices.text: That is a very interesting question, and I thank you for it, and many people have different views on this topic.
I would say no. The captain speaks for the players, not the donor; for instance, the players vote for theirs each year.
It depends. Sometimes sponsors are helpful, and sometimes they are not, so it is honestly very difficult to say either way, in my opinion.

feedback.es: Toma postura (no), la razona (el capitán habla por los jugadores) y da un ejemplo. Las otras se quedan en cortesía o en «it depends».

origin.text: Interviewer: What if the sponsor wanted to choose the team captain?

prompt.es: Completa: «Pondría el límite en que el patrocinador elija a los jugadores.»

feedback.es: Draw the line at + acción es la colocación fija para fijar el límite que no se cruza.

origin.text: I would gladly take the money and help the club, but I would ___ the line at letting the sponsor choose the players.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la respuesta de Mia sobre su postura.

choices.text: That it is firm and without conditions: she backs the plan whatever happens.
That it is reluctant: she agrees only because the sponsor insists.
That it is firm but conditional: students must pay nothing extra.

feedback.es: Mia dice «yes» y fija una condición: que el sobrecoste no recaiga en los estudiantes. Es firme pero condicionada: no es un apoyo incondicional ni una aceptación forzada.

origin.audio: Halfway through her presentation, a teacher asked Mia whether she would still support the plan if it cost twice as much. Mia smiled, said that it was a fair point and that she needed a moment. Then she answered: yes, provided that the extra cost came from the sponsor and not from students, because it comes down to who pays for the risk.

prompt.es: ¿Qué corrección aplica la estructura completa a esta respuesta?

choices.text: On balance I would accept, because the club needs funds; for instance, our nets are broken. That said, I would set a condition.
I would accept, because the club needs funds. That is my position, and I will not change it, whatever anyone says.
Sponsors have advantages, and they also have disadvantages, but on balance both sides of the question are equally important to consider.

feedback.es: Toma postura, la razona, da un ejemplo y añade un matiz. La segunda da postura y razón, pero no ofrece ningún ejemplo ni matiz, y la tercera no decide nada.

origin.text: Well, it is difficult. Some people like sponsors, and others do not, and there are good points on both sides, and in my opinion it is hard to say.

prompt.es: Escribe en inglés: «Dicho esto, pondría el límite en la publicidad durante los partidos.»

answer.text: That said, I would draw the line at advertising during matches.
accepted: That said, I would draw the line at advertising during matches.
That said, I would set a limit: no advertising during matches.
However, I would draw the line at advertising during matches.

feedback.es: That said abre el matiz y draw the line at + nombre fija el límite que no se cruza.

origin.text: Dicho esto, pondría el límite en la publicidad durante los partidos.

es: Demostrar el nivel C1 en una tarea integrada: analizar un caso, negociar una solución con tacto y resumirla con matices para otro lector.

vocabulary.es: en aras de, por el bien de

teaching.en: Each resident who wants to raise a concern deserves a serious answer, so the council cannot simply go ahead with the plan.
teaching.es: Cada vecino que quiera plantear una preocupación merece una respuesta seria, así que el municipio no puede seguir adelante sin más con el plan.
teaching.explanationEs: Raise a concern = plantear una preocupación. Go ahead with = seguir adelante con algo ya previsto.
segments: Each resident who wants to raise a concern deserves a serious
answer, so the council cannot simply go ahead with the plan.
teaching.audioText: Each resident who wants to raise a concern deserves a serious answer, so the council cannot simply go ahead with the plan.

teaching.en: Before it decides, the council must weigh the options, since every outcome helps one group and worries another.
teaching.es: Antes de decidir, el municipio debe sopesar las opciones, ya que cada resultado ayuda a un grupo y preocupa a otro.
teaching.explanationEs: Weigh the options = comparar ventajas y riesgos. Outcome = resultado final de un proceso.
segments: Before it decides, the council must weigh the options,
since every outcome helps one group and worries another.
teaching.audioText: Before it decides, the council must weigh the options, since every outcome helps one group and worries another.

teaching.en: A compromise is easier to hammer out when both sides say what they need, not merely what they want.
teaching.es: Un compromiso es más fácil de cerrar cuando ambas partes dicen lo que necesitan, y no solo lo que quieren.
teaching.explanationEs: Hammer out = negociar hasta lograr un acuerdo. Necesidad frente a deseo: la base de un compromiso.
segments: A compromise is easier to hammer out when both sides
say what they need, not merely what they want.
teaching.audioText: A compromise is easier to hammer out when both sides say what they need, not merely what they want.

teaching.en: To make a concession, offer something cheap for you but valuable for them, such as ten parking spaces on the lot.
teaching.es: Para hacer una concesión, ofrece algo barato para ti pero valioso para ellos, como diez plazas de estacionamiento en el solar.
teaching.explanationEs: Make a concession = ceder algo para avanzar. Lot = solar, terreno vacío.
segments: To make a concession, offer something cheap for you but valuable
for them, such as ten parking spaces on the lot.
teaching.audioText: To make a concession, offer something cheap for you but valuable for them, such as ten parking spaces on the lot.

teaching.en: In the interests of fairness, summarise the outcome by saying who gains, who loses and what concern remains.
teaching.es: Por el bien de la imparcialidad, resume el resultado diciendo quién gana, quién pierde y qué preocupación sigue abierta.
teaching.explanationEs: In the interests of = en aras de. Summarise = resumir (no resume, que significa «reanudar»).
segments: In the interests of fairness, summarise the outcome by
saying who gains, who loses and what concern remains.
teaching.audioText: In the interests of fairness, summarise the outcome by saying who gains, who loses and what concern remains.

teaching.en: To summarise with nuance, use seem, may or appear: the outcome seems acceptable to most residents, though not to everyone.
teaching.es: Para resumir con matiz, usa seem, may o appear: el resultado parece aceptable para la mayoría de los vecinos, aunque no para todos.
teaching.explanationEs: Un resumen matizado evita «todos» y «nadie»: cuantifica y deja abierto lo que sigue pendiente.
segments: To summarise with nuance, use seem, may or appear: the
outcome seems acceptable to most residents, though not to everyone.
teaching.audioText: To summarise with nuance, use seem, may or appear: the outcome seems acceptable to most residents, though not to everyone.

prompt.es: ¿Qué describe mejor el punto de partida del caso?

choices.text: One group wants the lot, and the other opposes any change at all.
Two legitimate aims want the same space, and both groups worry about noise.
The council has chosen a car park, and residents are appealing against it.

feedback.es: Hay dos objetivos legítimos para un solo solar y una preocupación común por el ruido. Ningún grupo se opone a todo cambio, y el municipio no ha decidido nada.

hint.es: Busca lo que comparten los dos grupos además de lo que los separa.

origin.text: Case file: The empty lot on Linden Street belongs to the council. Mia's group wants a community garden. Tom's group wants a car park, because nearby shops have lost customers. Both groups have raised concerns about noise.

prompt.es: Completa: «Pasaron dos horas intentando cerrar un acuerdo aceptable para ambos.»

feedback.es: Hammer out an agreement es la colocación natural para negociar con esfuerzo hasta cerrar un acuerdo; work out y thrash out también son posibles.

hint.es: Es el verbo de golpear, usado en sentido figurado para acuerdos.

origin.text: Mia and Tom spent two hours trying to ___ out an agreement that both groups could accept. By the end, each had given up something.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Veo tu preocupación, pero lo veo de forma algo distinta.»

answer.text: I see your concern but I see it slightly differently

feedback.es: La primera parte reconoce la preocupación del otro y slightly differently discrepa con tacto, sin decir que está equivocado.

hint.es: Primero se reconoce; después se discrepa con una fórmula suave.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo maneja Mia el desacuerdo con Tom.

choices.text: She agrees that parking matters more and drops her garden proposal.
She acknowledges his concern politely but refuses to consider any compromise.
She acknowledges his concern, disagrees tactfully and offers a conditional compromise.

feedback.es: Mia reconoce, discrepa con «slightly differently» y propone un compromiso con condición (provided that). No retira su propuesta ni rechaza todo compromiso.

origin.audio: At the meeting, Tom said that parking mattered more than flowers. Mia replied that she understood his concern, but that she saw it slightly differently: a garden would bring customers as well. Then she suggested a small garden on half of the lot, provided that ten parking spaces stayed. Tom hesitated, and then nodded.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la función que cumple en la negociación.

pairs: To summarise, the plan seems fair

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función distinta: reconocer, discrepar con tacto, proponer con condición y resumir con matiz.

pairs: To summarise, the plan seems fair

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase resume los resultados con matiz?

choices.text: The plan seems acceptable to most residents, although the noise concern remains open.
Nearly all residents accept the plan, and the noise objection has been settled.
Six residents voted against, so the plan has clearly failed and must be dropped.

feedback.es: Usa seems y reconoce la reserva pendiente, sin generalizar. Decir que casi todos aceptan exagera (catorce de veintitrés), y seis votos en contra no bastan para declarar un fracaso.

origin.text: Residents' meeting notes: Fourteen residents voted for the garden and car park plan, six voted against, and three did not vote. The main objection was weekend noise.

prompt.es: Redacta un resumen matizado para el municipio: condición, reserva y plazo.

answer.text: Dear Council, To summarise, the residents of Linden Street have reached a compromise about the empty lot. At first, Mia wanted a garden, whereas Tom wanted parking, but both sides have moved towards the middle. They appear to agree on a small garden on half of the lot, provided that ten parking spaces stay and the garden is open to everyone. Admittedly, one concern remains: some residents fear that weekend noise may increase. Sara has therefore asked for a review in September, and most people seem to support that idea. The shopkeepers nearby have also welcomed the plan, since more visitors should bring more customers to their street. On balance, the outcome seems acceptable to most neighbours, although it may not satisfy everyone, and nobody has claimed a clear victory over the others. We would be grateful if the council could confirm its decision by 15 June, so that work can begin before the summer. Thank you very much for your time and attention. Kind regards, The Linden Street residents

Dear Council, In summary, the neighbours of Linden Street have agreed on a compromise for the empty lot. Mia first wanted a garden, while Tom preferred parking, but both have moved a little. A small garden will use half of the lot, as long as ten parking spaces remain and everyone can use the garden. One concern is still open: weekend noise might increase, so Sara has asked for a review in September, and several residents seem to agree with her. The nearby shops have welcomed the plan as well, because more visitors should bring more customers. Overall, the agreement seems fair to most residents, although it may not please everybody. We therefore ask the council to treat it as a balanced solution that both groups helped to build. Please confirm your decision before 15 June so that work can start early, and thank you very much for your time. Yours sincerely, The Linden Street residents

feedback.es: Un resumen final abre con To summarise, recoge el acuerdo y su condición, matiza con seems o may, nombra la preocupación pendiente y pide la decisión con un plazo exacto.

origin.text: Caso: solar vacío en la calle Linden. Mia quería un jardín; Tom, estacionamiento. Acuerdo de la reunión: jardín pequeño en la mitad del solar, diez plazas de estacionamiento y jardín abierto a todos los vecinos. Preocupación pendiente: el ruido de los fines de semana; Sara pidió revisar el acuerdo en septiembre. Los comerciantes de la zona acogen bien el plan. El municipio decidirá antes del 15 de junio. Escribe un resumen matizado y formal dirigido al municipio.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender el comentario final de la presidenta.

choices.text: That the chair was disappointed that nobody celebrated the outcome.
That the agreement worked because neither side claimed to have won.
That Mia and Tom accepted Sara's idea only under pressure from the chair.

feedback.es: Señalar que nadie habló de «victoria» sugiere que el acuerdo funcionó porque ninguna parte se sintió vencedora. No hay decepción de la presidenta, y Mia y Tom aceptaron de inmediato, sin presión.

origin.audio: Sara spoke last. She said that she liked the compromise, but that the noise of weekend events could spoil it for families living next to the lot, especially those with small children who go to bed early. She did not ask for anything to be removed. Instead, she proposed that the council review the agreement in September and adjust the opening hours if complaints continued. Mia and Tom both agreed at once, and the chair noted that nobody had used the word victory.

prompt.es: ¿Qué reescritura mantiene la objeción de Tom con tacto?

choices.text: With respect, you are wrong, and I think everybody at this meeting will agree with me about the garden and the car park.
I am so sorry, but perhaps, if you do not mind, there might be a small possibility of some sort of problem, I think.
I see the appeal of a garden, but I doubt it would work beside a car park; could we test half of the lot?

feedback.es: Reconoce lo atractivo de la idea, mantiene la duda y propone una prueba concreta. La segunda sigue siendo una objeción brusca y la tercera se disculpa tanto que pierde la objeción.

origin.text: Tom's message: That idea will never work. Nobody wants a garden next to a car park.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quien desee plantear una preocupación puede escribir al municipio.»

feedback.es: Raise a concern es la colocación habitual para plantear formalmente una preocupación; voice y express también son naturales.

origin.text: The council has opened a consultation on the lot. Any resident who wishes to ___ a concern can write to the council before the deadline.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la carta del municipio sobre las diez plazas.

choices.text: That they are not guaranteed if the costs increase.
That they will be reduced to eight in any case.
That residents will be asked to vote on them again.

feedback.es: «May be reduced to eight if the costs rise» deja las diez plazas condicionadas al coste. No están garantizadas, pero tampoco se reducirán a ocho en cualquier caso, ni se anuncia una nueva votación.

origin.audio: The council has written to residents to say that it will go ahead with the garden plan in the interests of the whole neighbourhood. It has noted, however, that the parking spaces may be reduced to eight if the building costs rise, and it invites anyone with a concern to write by the end of the month.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la última frase del informe?

choices.text: That the talks failed because nobody is happy.
That Tom's group was treated unfairly by the others.
That nobody being fully happy suggests a fair balance.
That the compromise will be reversed soon.

feedback.es: En un compromiso, que nadie quede del todo satisfecho puede indicar equilibrio: ambos ceden. El texto ya dice que las conversaciones han sido un éxito.

origin.text: Overall, the talks have been a success. Both groups feel that they were heard, although Tom's group would have preferred more parking and Mia's group a larger garden. Nobody is entirely satisfied, which, in a compromise, may be the best sign.

prompt.es: Escribe: «Para resumir, el resultado parece aceptable para la mayoría de los vecinos.»

answer.text: To summarise, the outcome seems acceptable to most residents.
accepted: To summarise, the outcome seems acceptable to most residents.
In summary, the outcome appears acceptable to most residents.
To summarise, the result seems acceptable to most of the residents.
